title: Lua: Improve Listener error handling
description:
Fix error handlers in Listener draw() and reset() to avoid doing
g_assert_not_reached() when getting LUA_ERRERR from lua_pcall().
Added error handler for Listener draw() callback.

Changed some capitalized words in various error message.

Closes #16974.

added 4 commits
  • bd1afdf1...73f3bc97 - 3 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 3264993f - Lua: Improve Listener error handling
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/782/diffs?diff_id=121432462&start_sha=bd1afdf1211c8e20d1fd44b6e44178e94b57ffd6)
changed the description
I suppose that `LUA_ERRERR` ("error while running the message handler.") was triggered, is it worth mentioning that in the commit message?
Yes I got `LUA_ERRERR`. Maybe we should also add this to the switch-case?
Probably yes, we already catch `LUA_ERRMEM` which is very rare. And in the unlikely case that we have an error in our message callback, it should not crash with `g_assert_not_reached()`.
I will add handling of `LUA_ERRERR` to the listener error handlers.
Is there any chance that this is running concurrent with some other dissector? If so, should this by avoided and `lua_pcall(tap->L,0,0,lua_gettop(tap->L)-1)` be used instead?

I would guess this may be called at any time. The current pattern is to do like I have done, do you think we should do this differently in draw and reset here?

Edit: I have changed to this pattern in the latest change.

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/782/diffs?diff_id=122068329&start_sha=7145a0d35a4c83a76497243baae8a8f17dfe94b3#957b5c4f7e6a3a9e06a4ae1c5a4f0b64aacaffa9_134_134)

Why drop the argument? Based on the documentation at https://www.lua.org/manual/5.2/manual.html#lua_pcall I think that the provided argument has to be returned?

> In case of runtime errors, this function will be called with the error message and its return value will be the message returned on the stack by lua_pcall.

Likewise for the draw error message callback below.
`tap_packet_cb_error_handler()` and all our other error handlers does `return 0` so I was following that pattern. Should we change everyone to `return 1`?
Possibly yes. Can you check the difference in returning `0` and returning `1`? I expect the original error message to be returned to the caller with `1`. I have no idea what happens with `0`.
I cannot observe any difference between using `0` and `1`, and all other error handlers have been using `0` since the beginning. I don't really know which value is correct here.

Lua: Improve Listener error handling

Fix error handlers in Listener draw() and reset() to avoid getting
LUA_ERRERR from lua_pcall(). Added error handler for Listener draw()
callback.

Handle LUA_ERRERR from lua_pcall() to avoid assert on this.
Changed some capitalized words in various error message.

Closes #16974.
